Let
\[
Y_i=2X_i-1\in\{-1,1\}.
\]
Then each \(Y_i\) has mean \(0\), and the \(6\)-wise independence assumption gives
\[
\mathbb E\prod_{i\in S}Y_i=0\qquad(1\le |S|\le 6).
\]

For \(y_i\in\{-1,1\}\), the indicator of the event that all \(Y_i\)’s are equal is
\[
\mathbf 1_{\{Y_1=\cdots=Y_8\}}
=\mathbf 1_{\{Y_i=1\ \forall i\}}+\mathbf 1_{\{Y_i=-1\ \forall i\}}.
\]
Using
\[
\mathbf 1_{\{Y_i=1\ \forall i\}}=2^{-8}\prod_{i=1}^8(1+Y_i),\qquad
\mathbf 1_{\{Y_i=-1\ \forall i\}}=2^{-8}\prod_{i=1}^8(1-Y_i),
\]
we get
\[
\mathbf 1_{\{Y_1=\cdots=Y_8\}}
=2^{-7}\sum_{\substack{S\subseteq\{1,\dots,8\}\\ |S|\text{ even}}}\prod_{i\in S}Y_i.
\]
Taking expectations, all even terms of sizes \(2,4,6\) vanish, so
\[
\mathbb P(Y_1=\cdots=Y_8)
=2^{-7}\left(1+\mathbb E\prod_{i=1}^8Y_i\right).
\]
Since \(\prod_{i=1}^8Y_i\le 1\),
\[
\mathbb P(X_1=\cdots=X_8)\le 2^{-7}(1+1)=\frac1{64}.
\]

This bound is attained by taking the uniform distribution on all binary strings of even parity:
\[
\mathbb P(X=x)=
\begin{cases}
2^{-7},& x_1+\cdots+x_8\equiv 0\pmod 2,\\
0,& x_1+\cdots+x_8\equiv 1\pmod 2.
\end{cases}
\]
Indeed, any choice of at most \(6\) coordinates has exactly half of its completions even and half odd, so every such subfamily is mutually independent and uniform. The two all-equal strings \(00000000\) and \(11111111\) both have even parity, so their total probability is
\[
2\cdot 2^{-7}=\frac1{64}.
\]

It remains to classify equality. Equality requires
\[
\mathbb E\prod_{i=1}^8Y_i=1,
\]
so
\[
\prod_{i=1}^8Y_i=1\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
Thus
\[
Y_8=Y_1Y_2\cdots Y_7.
\]
For \(Y_1,\dots,Y_7\), every nonempty product moment of size at most \(6\) is \(0\), and the size \(7\) product moment is
\[
\mathbb E(Y_1\cdots Y_7)=\mathbb E Y_8=0.
\]
Hence \(Y_1,\dots,Y_7\) are mutually independent fair signs. Therefore \(Y_8\) is forced to be their product, giving exactly the uniform even-parity distribution above.

\[
\boxed{\max \mathbb P(X_1=\cdots=X_8)=\frac1{64}}
\]

The unique maximizing joint distribution is the uniform distribution on the \(128\) binary strings with even parity.
